scope: Fresh review of official KDDI, Android, eSIM and A2A/Cloudflare primary sources for the contract-preparation objective. No provider contact, contract, booking, external app submission, carrier activation, or satellite field test was performed.
productDirection: RockstarOS service access is sold with either a physical SIM or eSIM through multiple channels; satellite-capable access is a separate carrier/device capability and does not store or install RockstarOS on a SIM.

findings.topic: KDDI consumer satellite offer and constraints
confirmed: UQ/povo/other-carrier customers may use the dedicated plan with a physical SIM or eSIM, subject to device and offer eligibility.
Current public page displays three free months from application, then JPY 1,650/month for other-carrier customers; terms may change and are not Rockstar wholesale/resale prices.
The plan describes a 1 GB/month terrestrial data allowance and says satellite usage is temporarily not counted against it.
Satellite access is limited to supported devices and selected app/data traffic; this is not evidence of arbitrary Internet or Rockstar API reachability.
Ordinary voice calling including 110/118/119 by voice is not supported over the satellite mode.
notProven: Rockstar wholesale/resale rights, eSIM provisioning API, account/subscriber activation API or carrier billing integration.
RockstarOS or any Rockstar cloud endpoint being allowlisted or accepted by KDDI.

confirmed: Eligible subscribers can send SOS information through approved apps and a messaging app to KDDI's SOS center, which relays reports to emergency-response agencies.
The relay is distinct from direct voice calling, is unavailable overseas, can be unavailable due to app/network conditions, and does not guarantee rescue.
notProven: Any Rockstar integration, eligibility, operational responsibility, or emergency-response service.

findings.topic: KDDI developer portal and handset/app acceptance
confirmed: The public developer portal lists Android 16+ and iOS 26+ for supported-app development and requires an eligible plan/SIM/eSIM plus supported handset.
The Android guide requires satellite-data manifest opt-in and advises satellite-aware UX; KDDI recommends clear connection, progress, retry and lightweight content behavior.
App-site listing is application-based. Published criteria include the app having been available for six months; the process describes separate coordination/agreement and may include NDA.
Pixel 10 is referenced in mock testing, while mock tests do not establish Rockstar field or RF acceptance.
notProven: Pixel 10 GL066 exact SKU/service-plan eligibility and Rockstar field behavior.
Rockstar app approval, listing, arbitrary cloud API traffic or resale access.

confirmed: Android apps do not use constrained satellite networks by default.
Apps must opt in and adapt data usage to constrained throughput/latency; satellite transport/network capabilities can be inspected on supported OS versions.
The app should reduce payloads, avoid large model/artifact downloads and handle queued/retried work clearly.
findings.implementationDecision: Keep satellite manifest opt-in disabled until Android 16 network detection, queue and retry caps, explicit status, small-result mode and device/network tests are implemented.

confirmed: As of the official page last updated 2026-09-30, standard-4 is limited to 4 vCPU, 12 GiB memory and 20 GB disk.
findings.implementationDecision: Continue to separate controller/orchestration from arbitrary agent or heavy/GPU inference runtime; do not assume the container tier is a GPU LLM worker.

confirmed: POST /orders transaction deducts the provider organization balance and returns an orderReference on the successful example; callers need to persist and reconcile that reference.
notProven: Client idempotency or recovery of a transaction when the create response is lost and no orderReference was received.

confirmed: The versioned A2A specification, rather than the moving main branch, is the contract source for task lifecycle, artifacts, transports and authentication.
findings.implementationDecision: Keep protocol state interoperable but enforce authorization, budget, expiry and credential scope in the Rockstar Broker; A2A state transitions alone do not grant Rockstar authority.

nextActions: Keep terrestrial, constrained direct-to-cell, external-terminal and offline connectivity as separate capability states.
Implement small status/approval/cancel/result requests and bounded retry behavior before Android satellite opt-in.
Verify exact SKU, Android version, plan, app traffic permissions, carrier contract/billing and field acceptance separately.
Keep KDDI's retail plan price and SOS relay outside Rockstar pricing and lifeline claims unless explicit agreements and acceptance exist.
